tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

I can fix that myself with a small Kotlin change, but Luna is editing the same worktree right now on the R1-R4 queue, so I'm weighing where to make the edit so it doesn't collide with her work.

I'm weighing whether to push the Kotlin fix onto Luna's branch, since that would likely get rejected as non-fast-forward while she's still working. Instead I'll develop the fix in my validation worktree on a separate branch, iterating on the build and emulator, then apply it onto the p1 branch after her queue finishes.

I'm working out the Android fix: the crash comes from touching the insets controller before the decor view exists, so I'd call `findViewById(android.R.id.content)` first to force decor creation and then use `WindowCompat.getInsetsController` for the status bar appearance. I also want to replace the deprecated status and navigation bar colours with a window background set to the surface colour, since those calls do nothing under edge-to-edge.

Rework step R3 of 4: rendered geometry tests and review screenshots. Finish it fully, commit, push, end the turn with a short status. If R2 left anything unfinished or red, finish that first.

Why your two rendered tests failed with a 0×0 button: the browser preview mounts two `App` instances (see `src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue`); the inactive workspace is hidden, so its buttons measure 0×0. Scope every query to the visible workspace, for example `.workspace-panel:not([inert]) .app`, as the existing rendered tests do (read `tests/browsing/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` and `tests/reader/reader.rendered.test.ts` for the helpers and conventions, including how they wait for the list and open a conversation).

1. Rewrite `tests/layout/mobile-shell.rendered.test.ts` as readable multi-line code. Cases, each at 412×915 and 360×800 with the phone preset:
   - Inbox: `data-layout` is `compact`; `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and no element inside the active `.app` has a right edge beyond the viewport; the workspace strip, top bar, header strip and list do not overlap each other vertically; the bottom region is inside the viewport; every button in the top bar and the bar row is at least 48×48; the rail is not displayed.
   - Scroll clearance: scroll the list to its end; the last row's bottom edge is above the top of the bottom region.
   - Notes stay visible: the preview tag (`data-test="preview-banner"`) has a non-zero box, is inside the viewport and overlaps no button.
   - Reader: open the first conversation; `reader-close` is inside the top bar at the left; all buttons of `reader-toolbar` are inside `mobile-reader-actions`, each at least 48×48, no two overlap, all inside the viewport; the navigation is gone; the reader's last message can scroll clear of the bottom region.
   - Back to the list: activating `reader-close` returns to the list and the navigation is back.
   - Regular: a separate harness at the default 1200×800 asserts `data-layout="regular"`, the rail and contact column are displayed, and no mobile element exists.
2. Fix the layout, not the assertions, until these pass. Then run the whole rendered suite: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome mise run test:rendered > /tmp/mobile-p1-rendered.log 2>&1; tail -25 /tmp/mobile-p1-rendered.log`. The 49 existing tests must still pass.
3. Review screenshots: a separate file `tests/layout/mobile-screenshots.rendered.test.ts` (skipped unless both `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME` and `EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR` are set; not part of `test:rendered`) that drives the active workspace and saves: `inbox.png`, `inbox-scrolled-end.png`, `reader.png`, `reader-scrolled-end.png`, `destinations-overlay.png` (menu button), `palette.png` (open it from the Destinations overlay or by its action), `compose.png` (compose button), `search.png` (Search in the nav), `drafts.png`, `reminders.png`, `account.png` (Account in the nav), and with a second harness at 1200×800 `desktop-inbox.png` and `desktop-reader.png`. Wait for each surface to settle before capturing. Add a `mise` task `screenshots:mobile` that runs it and document it in `docs/development.md`.
4. Run it with `EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os-mobile-review/p1` and list the files written (`ls -la`). Do not open the images.
5. Commit and push.

I’ll complete the rendered work against the active workspace only, using the established Chrome harness and fixture interaction patterns. I won’t open screenshots. I’ll fix the frame if the geometry checks reveal layout issues, then run the full rendered suite and capture the review set.

items.text: R3 is still incomplete. The active-workspace rendered tests now pass at 412×915 and cover reader teleports and regular mode, but the 360×800 case still finds inbox elements beyond the viewport. The full rendered suite and screenshot capture have not been completed, and no R3 commit or push was made.

Rework step R4 of 4: documents and PR description. If R3 left anything unfinished or red, finish that first.

1. Bring `docs/ux-14-mobile-shell.md`, `DESIGN.md` ("Compact layout (phone)") and `docs/adr/0003-mobile-layout.md` in line with what is now built: the frame structure (top bar, header strip, bottom region with context slot and bar row), the hosts (`backHost`, `actionsHost`), the tokens with their values, `--mobile-bottom-clearance`, the one allowed media query, the Android Back bridge, and what is explicitly left to later phases. Write them as short, plain prose in the style of the existing `docs/ux-*.md` files.
2. Final checks, with exact counts: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and the full rendered suite.
3. Update the description of PR #75 (`gh pr edit 75 -R BbrSofiane/email-os --body-file <file>`): what changed, decisions, validation counts, and "Android build and emulator checks are done by the coordinator". Push everything.
4. Final message: head SHA, the counts, the list of screenshot files, and anything you could not make pass, with the failing output.

R3 is still red at 360px, so I’ll resolve that first by constraining the preview’s flex workspace and verifying the rendered geometry at both phone widths. Then I’ll bring the short UX/ADR/design documents and PR body up to date and run the final checks. I will not run Android build or cargo.

R3 is still red at 360px: the rendered test reports inbox descendants extending to about 403px. I tried constraining the preview workspace to the viewport, but that did not resolve it. I haven’t completed R3, so I’m not proceeding with R4’s documentation, final checks, or PR update. No commit or push was made for these attempted changes.

content.thinking:

Then I'll hand it the more mechanical feature work with tighter specs.
